build.summary: Built diag-lv-aorta-render. A new module, src/render/xray/lvGram.ts, now draws ventriculograms and aortograms. It replaces the old uniformly filling ventriculogram ellipsoid in sceneBuilder. The LV cavity is the fitted LV of heartShape shrunk to the endocardium. It moves with the same least-squares affine fit as the drawn wall (heartShape.ventricleAffine) and narrows to the mitral annulus at the base. It is drawn as one ribbon tube of elliptical cross-sections with four walls, laid out so that RAO 30 profiles the anterior and inferior walls and LAO 60 cranial 20 the septal and posterolateral walls. Each wall moves inwards in systole by its segment's excursion on the patient clock's envelope. The classes are normal, hypokinetic, akinetic and dyskinetic (new heartMotion WALL_MOTION_SCALE, LV_ENDOCARDIUM, endocardialRadius). Segment state comes from the case (SceneInput.lvGram) or from the engine: the new PatientEngine.lvWallState() feeds lvGram.segmentsFromEngine, which maps regional ischaemia and necrosis to segments. Opacification follows the injection trace through a beat-by-beat compartment model (LV with mixing over beats, LA, aorta, RV). Its flows come from the cavity's own volume curve. MR fills the LA by grade and AR fills the LV from a root injection by grade, following Oxford's density definitions. Ectopic beats and catheter-induced MR or AR add regurgitation. Also implemented: a myocardial stain with a pericardial crescent, an apical thrombus filling defect, takotsubo ballooning, a VSD jet into an RV cavity, and the anomalous circumflex dot (its retro-aortic segment runs along the RAO 30 view axis). The aortogram fills the root, ascending aorta, arch and its branches, with graft stumps carrying marker rings and a domed AS valve with a systolic jet. iliofemoralExtras(model, trace, full) gives an iliofemoral run for SceneInput.extras. BolusView gains `aortogram`, SceneInput gains `lvGram`, and SceneResult gains an optional `lvGram` (chamber contrast). Renders without an LV or root injection are unchanged: the offscreen realism frames are byte-identical to the baseline, and compare_sets reports no rows lost or gained.

src/render/xray/XrayRenderer.ts buildTubes: its sample decimation (keep a sample only when it is at least half the projected width from the last kept one) is tuned for vessels. A chamber-aware rule would need a renderer package.
build.notes:
Snapshots of the four pre-existing listed files are in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/diag-lv-aorta-render/ with .started (14:43, 9 Oct). Only listed files and new test files were edited.

Shared engine: PatientEngine gains only a read-only lvWallState() and the exported types LvWallRegion and LvWallState. Defaults are unchanged and the patient, contrast-budget, hypotension and transducer tests pass. heartShapes() output is unchanged: it now reads heartChambers(), which builds the same ellipsoids. heartMotion only gains exports.

Module-text sources used:
- The wall-motion classes, the views that profile each wall, thrombus, takotsubo, the anomalous circumflex dot and VSD in LAO cranial come from src/content/manual/cath-handbook/04-cardiac-catheterisation.ts, "Reading the ventriculogram" and the views table.
- MR grades I-IV are from the Oxford table in the same lesson, and the Sellers grade 4 pulmonary-vein reflux from the paragraph after that table.
- AR grades are from the check at line ~1724 and from 07-tavi.ts.
- MAPSE values are reused from heartMotion's existing Ochs 2017 constants.
Everything else is a MODEL PARAMETER (listed in outOfScope).

Engine to segment mapping: a region pointing towards the apex counts for the apical segment (blended between 0.6 and 0.9 of the long-axis component); the rest of it counts for the nearest wall direction. With the default network, an LAD occlusion gives anterior and apical akinesis or hypokinesis, and an RCA occlusion gives inferior.

Visual notes from the captures: the cavity is now an ovoid that narrows at the base, with the LVOT as a short tube to the valve. LV density falls over 3-4 beats after the push because each beat ejects about 60%. No real ventriculogram or aortogram targets exist in the scorecard, so the look still needs licensed reference images or expert review, as the plan says. The aortic arch lies above the field when the table is centred on the heart. The VSD's RV opacification is faint (shunt 0.25, RV mixing 120 mL).

Browser work used only a new tab (tab-62), which was closed at the end. Its viewport emulation was reset to desktop first.

findings.where: src/render/xray/lvGram.ts:557-628 (lvGramContrast: t0 = max(pushStart, t - HISTORY_S), stainMl integrated only inside that window); src/render/xray/sceneBuilder.ts chamberRun block
findings.problem: The myocardial stain does not persist. stainMl is summed only over the 30 s history window, so when the window passes pushEnd the stain falls to zero, although stainTauS is 240 s. I measured this with {stain:{segment:'inferior'}}, 30 mL at 12 mL/s: stain 0.93 at 20 s, 0.89 at 30 s, 0.59 at 32 s and 0.000 at 33 s. In the live lab it is worse. lvGramFrame runs only while a bolus exists, and labSession drops the bolus at pushEnd + CONTRAST_CLEAR_S (3.5 s). The stain therefore disappears about 3.5 s after the push, while the LV is still faintly opacified. The defining sign of a stain (it persists after the cavity has cleared) cannot be shown, and the test at t = 11 s passes only because it calls lvGramFrame directly.
findings.fix: In lvGramContrast, compute the injected wall volume from the whole trace and not from the window. For example, `stainMl = spec.stain ? volumeUpTo(trace, Math.min(o.t, trace.pushEnd ?? o.t)) * contrastFraction : 0`, or integrate tr.q*tr.c over [trace.pushStart, o.t] in a separate loop that ignores HISTORY_S. In sceneBuilder, also draw the stain when there is no bolus. Add an optional `stain.sinceS` (seconds since the staining push) and `stain.strength` to LvGramSpec. When `inp.lvGram?.stain` is set and chamberRun is false, push only the stain bone and crescent tube, using strength × exp(-sinceS / stainTauS). Factor that out of lvGramFrame as `stainPrims(H, m, spec, full, toHeart)`. Add a buildXrayScene test: with bolus null and lvGram.stain {sinceS: 20}, the stain bone is present.

findings.problem: Every frame re-integrates the compartment model from the push to now in 10 ms steps. Each step calls cavityVolumeMl, which allocates 28 sliceRadii objects, plus a traceAt object. Per-frame cost therefore grows with time since the press. I measured lvGramFrame (vite-node, nominal heart, MR II) at 0.55 ms at t = 3 s, 0.93 ms at 8 s, 1.54 ms at 15 s and 3.13 ms at 30 s, with about 87k short-lived objects per frame at 30 s. The same frame also rebuilds cavityProfile (28 Record objects), calls heartChambers, which repeats the fitVentricles that sceneBuilder already did for heartShapes, and runs ventricleAffine and rvCavity, each another affine fit. This breaks the rule of no per-frame allocations in render paths, on a machine that already stalls under load.
findings.fix: (1) In cavityProfile, tabulate the volume curve once: `volTable = Float64Array(65)` of cavityVolumeMl(p, k/64). Have volAt interpolate it, and compute edv and esv from it. (2) Memoise cavityProfile in a WeakMap keyed on H, with an inner Map keyed on a stable spec key (JSON of the fields it reads). (3) Make the integration incremental. Keep a module-level `WeakMap<InjectionTrace, {site, specKey, tLast, nLv, nPool, nLa, nAo, nRv, stainMl, vPrev}>` and advance from tLast to o.t. Restart from pushStart only when o.t < tLast or the site or spec key changes. Then HISTORY_S is no longer needed. Use a scalar traceAt lookup (index = floor(tau/dt)) instead of the object return in the loop. (4) Let lvGramFrame take the chambers that sceneBuilder already has, or cache heartChambers per (H, m), so the LV fit is not repeated. Add a test that 300 successive frames at 1/30 s, from t = 0 to 10 s, match a fresh integration at t = 10 s within 1e-6.

findings.problem: The outflow-tract tube starts 1 mm inside the cavity's first cross-section (from = s0.axisPt + 0.35·r·e1 − 1 mm·L) at full c.lv. Where it overlaps the cavity tube the iodine is counted twice. In the builder's own capture datasets/tmp/captures/lvgram_rao30_v2.png, all four frames show a darker, angular block where the cavity base meets the LVOT, which does not look like a ventriculogram.
findings.fix: Start the LVOT at or beyond the cavity's basal surface: from = s0.c − L·(2 mm) − e1·0 so that it lies outside the first slice, and give its first sample zero iodine (`mu: [[0,0,0],[0,full*c.lv,0],[0,full*c.lv*0.95,0]]`) so it fades in. Alternatively, prepend the LVOT samples to the cavity tube's own path, so one ribbon runs from the valve to the apex with no overlap. Re-capture RAO 30 to confirm.

findings.where: src/render/xray/lvGram.ts:339 (cavityTube thinDir), 760 (ellBone ax), 795 (thrombus ax), 839/846-848 (stain ax, crescent thin dirs), 502 (rvCavity ax)
findings.problem: Positions are mapped to world through toHeart/toAortic. Those include toWorld = rotateZ(model.aortaTiltRad), 5 to 8 degrees in the library cases. The directions are not mapped: the cavity's thin-axis dirs (cav.e1/e2), the axes of the LA, LAA, RV, thrombus and stain ellipsoids, and the crescent's thin dirs all stay in the aortic frame. So the elliptical cross-section and every chamber ellipsoid are turned by the tilt relative to their own centres. Vessel thin dirs are computed in world (minorAxisDir uses `place`).
findings.fix: In lvGramFrame, define `const z = o.toHeart(v(0,0,0)); const dirW = (d: Vec3) => sub(o.toHeart(d), z);`. This is the linear part of toWorld, because heartShift cancels. Use it for every `ax` entry pushed to bones (ellBone, thrombus, stain) and for the thin dirs: pass dirW into cavityTube/cavityTubes (`thinDir.push(dirW(a <= b ? cav.e1 : cav.e2))`) and into the crescent's dirs. Add a test with a model whose aortaTiltRad ≠ 0 checking that the cavity tube's thin dir is perpendicular to its world tangent within 1e-6.

findings.problem: The test 'without an LV or root injection the scene is unchanged' is weak and partly tautological. Line 362 compares heartShapes(H, mES) with itself. Lines 360-361 compare only tube and bone counts, so a changed value with the same count would pass. The heartShape refactor (heartShapes now reads heartChambers) is therefore not checked by any test in the package.
findings.fix: Replace the counts with deep equality: `expect(b.scene.tubes).toEqual(a.scene.tubes); expect(b.scene.bones).toEqual(a.scene.bones);`. Replace line 362 with a real check: either inline fixture values of heartShapes(makeHeart(1), mES) c/half for the LV, LA and root recorded from the snapshot version (datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/diag-lv-aorta-render/src/render/xray/heartShape.ts), or assert that each heartShapes primitive's c equals the matching heartChambers field's c (lv, rv, ra, la, laa, rvot, pad, root).

The module text says the two schemes differ and that the reader must 'say which scheme you used'. Drawing Sellers' sign on every Oxford grade IV merges the two schemes, and a trainee would learn that Oxford IV means pulmonary-vein reflux.

Otherwise keep the comment and rename the condition so that it states it shows the Sellers feature, and record the choice in the facts file. Add a test that Oxford IV draws no reflux tubes and Sellers 4 draws four.

findings.problem: ventricleAffine returns the shared module-level IDENTITY array at rest. Any caller that mutates the result, for example by composing in place, would corrupt every later rest-state fit.

review.verdict:
Accept after two fixes. The design is largely in place. lvGram.ts implements the segmented endocardial cavity riding on the LV affine fit; the wall-motion classes, which are profiled correctly in RAO 30 and LAO 60 cranial 20; the beat-by-beat compartment model with MR and AR grades; the mapping from engine ischaemia to segments; the stain, thrombus, takotsubo, VSD and anomalous-circumflex dot; the aortogram with graft stumps and the AS jet; and the iliofemoral extras. The sceneBuilder change is confined to LV and root injections. The engine change only adds a read-only lvWallState(), heartMotion only adds exports, and the heartShape refactor keeps heartShapes identical, so shared defaults are unchanged.

I re-ran the package tests: lvGram.test.ts, lvGram.tips.test.ts and lvWall.test.ts, 22 passed. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` is clean. The diffs against the snapshots contain only this package's changes. The other recently modified files under src (haemo/avCrossing, ValvePanel, CatheterPanel, aorticStenosis.launch, the bifurcation bench files, PciBench) belong to other packages. The acceptance tests are meaningful: the akinetic anterior area change in RAO 30 is under 10%, dyskinesis moves outward, MR III is close to the LV's density and MR I clears each beat. No ground truth reaches a live screen (segmentClasses is for the answer key only). Clinical constants are taken from the module text or labelled MODEL PARAMETER in code.

The two fixes needed:
1. The myocardial stain does not persist. It is summed only inside a 30 s history window, so it drops to zero about 30 s after the push (measured: 0.89 at 30 s, 0 at 33 s). In the live lab it vanishes when the bolus ends, 3.5 s after the push.
2. Every frame re-integrates the compartment model from the push. That costs 0.55 to 3.1 ms per frame and creates tens of thousands of short-lived objects, against the rule of no per-frame allocations in render paths.

Minor issues:
- The LVOT tube overlaps the cavity base and double-counts iodine; it shows as a dark angular block in the RAO 30 captures.
- Ellipsoid axes and thin-axis directions are not rotated by the aortic tilt, while their centres are.
- The 'unchanged scene' test compares only counts and includes a tautological line.
- Grade IV MR draws the Sellers pulmonary-vein reflux on what the code presents as Oxford grades.
- There is no docs/realism/facts entry for the model parameters.
- The live wiring is missing: FluoroView and labSession pass no lvGram and no aortogram flag. Contrary to the builder's note, other packages do list FluoroView.tsx (for example diag-injection-run-quality), so the plan should give this wiring to diag-lv-aorta-task or coordinate it with that package.
- The tips test builds its context by hand, so the 'in a scenario that exercises it' part of the tips acceptance is still unmet; diag-lv-aorta-task should add the scenario-driven version.
- ventricleAffine returns a shared, mutable identity array.

The browser acceptance is only partly met, because no live path yet supplies a case pattern.

rejected: Finding 6 (FluoroView/labSession never pass SceneInput.lvGram or aortogram, and the bolus ends at pushEnd + 3.5 s): correct, but src/ui/sim/FluoroView.tsx and src/ui/sim/labSession.ts are outside this package. A plan amendment is needed so that diag-lv-aorta-task, or diag-injection-run-quality in coordination, owns them, with these acceptance items: (a) pass lvGram: segmentsFromEngine(tree.heart, engine.lvWallState(), caseSpec) when b.lv or b.aortogram is set; (b) bolusFor() returns aortogram: true for a pigtail root injection; (c) keep the chamber run going until SceneResult.lvGram lv, la and aorta are all below about 0.002; (d) after the run, pass lvGram.stain.sinceS so the scene draws the clearing stain (the new path in sceneBuilder); (e) a browser check at RAO 30 with an LAD-occlusion case and no __sceneOverrides.

Finding 7 (docs/realism/facts/diag-lv-aorta-render.md is missing): correct, but the facts path is not in this package's file list. diag-lv-aorta-task or a facts-audit package should create it. It should list WALL_MOTION_SCALE, LV_ENDOCARDIUM, LV_CAVITY, BASE_NARROWING, WALL_PHI, APICAL_FROM, MR_GRADES, AR_GRADES, LV_CIRCULATION, AORTA_PATH, ARCH_BRANCHES, ANOMALOUS_CX, ILIOFEMORAL, regionScale, the rvCavity offsets, the LVOT ellipsoid (LV_CAVITY.lvotRadiusMm, starting 2 mm beyond the base) and the 0.01 rounding in segmentsFromEngine, each as MODEL PARAMETER. fix.notes:
Applied 7 of the 10 findings and rejected 3 because their files belong to other packages. All edits are in this package's files. Only lvGram.ts, lvGram.test.ts, sceneBuilder.ts and heartShape.ts changed; heartMotion.ts and engine.ts are untouched.

1. Stain persistence (major), fixed.
   - The stain is now built from all contrast pushed into the LV over the whole run (`wallMl` in the saved state), not a 30 s window. The window constant HISTORY_S is gone. The stain decays from pushEnd with stainTauS.
   - Added `LvGramSpec.stain.sinceS`, and new exports `stainPrims(input, strength)` (factored out of lvGramFrame) and `stainAfterRun(spec)`.
   - In sceneBuilder, when there is no LV or root run and `inp.lvGram.stain.sinceS` is set, the scene draws the stain bone and crescent at strength × exp(-sinceS/stainTauS). Without `sinceS` nothing is drawn, so the stain cannot appear before the push.
   - New tests: the stain is still above 0.9 of its 20 s value at 40 s, and the scene draws it with no bolus (sinceS 20) but not at sinceS 2000.

2. Per-frame cost (major), fixed.
   - cavityProfile is memoised per HeartFrame and spec key, and tabulates its volume curve once (65 samples; `profileVolume` interpolates it). edv and esv come from the table.
   - lvGramContrast integrates on a fixed 10 ms grid from pushStart. Its state is kept per trace and per flow-relevant spec key in a WeakMap, so each frame only advances it.
   - It restarts when time goes back. Grid steps beyond the trace's recorded samples during a live push are recomputed each frame and not kept.
   - The trace lookup inside the loop no longer allocates (`sampleTrace`).
   - heartShape now caches the affine fits and heartChambers per (H, Motion object), so lvGramFrame, laCavity and rvCavity reuse the fits heartShapes already did that frame. fitVentricles uses the cached ventricleAffine.
   - segmentsFromEngine rounds each segment scale to 0.01, so slowly changing ischaemia does not change the profile key every frame.
   - Measured (vite-node, MR II): about 0.04 to 0.08 ms per frame at t = 3, 8, 15 and 30 s. It no longer grows with time.
   - New test: 301 frames at 1/30 s from 0 to 10 s match a fresh integration within 1e-6, for MR, AR and VSD at both the lv and root sites.

3. LVOT double count (minor), fixed, but not as the reviewer suggested.
   - The suggested change (start beyond the base, first sample with zero iodine) still drew a dark angular block at the valve end. A short, wide ribbon tube seen almost end-on in RAO 30 shows flat end caps.
   - The outflow tract is now a tapering ellipsoid bone from 2 mm beyond the cavity's base to the valve, at full × c.lv. Its tapered ends avoid the double count and it has no flat caps.
   - I re-rendered RAO 30 in a background tab of the running dev server (rendered offscreen, no __sceneOverrides) and the angular block is gone. The images were viewed only, not saved to datasets/tmp/captures.
   - The cavity's straight mitral-plane base is unchanged.
   - New test: the outflow bone sits on the valve side of the base plane, its basal tip stops at the base, and its other end reaches the valve.

4. Directions under aortic tilt (minor), fixed.
   - New export `directionMap(toW)` gives the linear part of the frame-to-world map.
   - It is now applied to the cavity tube's thin directions (new optional `dirToWorld` argument on cavityTube and cavityTubes), the LA, LAA and RV ellipsoid axes, the thrombus and stain axes, the crescent's thin directions, the LVOT midpoint offset, and the root and AS-dome axes.
   - I also applied it to the iliofemoral pelvis box, which had the same problem.
   - New test with a 7 degree rotation: the thin direction stays perpendicular to the world tangent within 1e-6, and the thrombus axis lies along the world long axis.

5. Weak "scene unchanged" test (minor), fixed.
   - It now uses deep `toEqual` on tubes and bones, with a priming build so both scenes follow a frame at the same time.
   - New test: heartShapes matches fixture centres and half sizes for all 10 shapes, within 1e-5. I recorded the fixtures by running the pre-package snapshot of heartShape.ts (datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/diag-lv-aorta-render) through vite-node. The test also checks that a fresh Motion object (no cached fit) gives the same shapes.

8. Sellers versus Oxford (minor), fixed.
   - Added `mrScheme?: 'oxford' | 'sellers'`, default 'oxford'. Pulmonary-vein reflux is drawn only for Sellers grade 4.
   - New test: Oxford IV draws no reflux tubes and Sellers 4 draws four.

10. Shared IDENTITY (minor), fixed. It is frozen, and `Affine` is now typed `readonly (readonly number[])[]`.

The three rejected findings (lab wiring in FluoroView and labSession, the facts file, the scenario-driven tips test) are correct but need files outside this package. The details and proposed acceptance items are in `rejected`. The caches and the frozen IDENTITY keep render outputs numerically the same.

fix2.notes:
I changed only package files: src/render/xray/lvGram.ts, src/render/xray/sceneBuilder.ts and src/render/xray/lvGram.test.ts.

Finding 1 (polygonal outline): confirmed and fixed inside the package.
- **Interpolation:** sliceAt now uses a Catmull-Rom spline over the 28 profile slices, in theta = asin(u) where those slices are evenly spaced. Radii are clamped at zero, the axis point is exact and the centre is computed from the radii.
- **Sampling:** cavityTubes samples evenly in theta, at most CAVITY_DRAW.sampleMm = 1.25 mm apart along the axis (24 to 160 samples). This is a MODEL PARAMETER.
- **Workaround for the renderer's sample dropping:** XrayRenderer.buildTubes has a documented shell rule: the first tube drawn on a points array decides the samples for every tube that shares it. cavityTubes therefore lists a zero-iodine guide tube first (r 0.05 mm, sharing the cavity's pts array; isCavityGuide identifies it), so every sample is kept.
- **End-on fallback:** if the long axis is within asin(0.5) of the ray, using the world view direction now passed from sceneBuilder, the old radius spacing is kept with no guide. This avoids the ribbon folding the drop rule exists to prevent.
- **Tests:** the outline's largest turn per sample (below 0.9 of the length) is under 12 degrees and under half of the old spacing's, in RAO 30 ED, RAO 30 ES with anterior akinesis, and LAO 60 cranial 20 ES. The remaining bend is the profile's own curvature: halving the step roughly halved the turn. A further test checks that the spline reproduces the profile slices exactly. The area-change tests are unchanged and still pass.
- **outOfScope for the renderer's owner:** a `keepSamples?: boolean` opt-out on TubeSpec (thorax.ts) honoured by XrayRenderer.buildTubes would replace the guide.

Finding 2 (LV injection puff): confirmed and fixed.
- **What it draws:** the compartment model's unmixed pool (LvGramContrast gains poolMl) is drawn as a puff of three nested ellipsoids along the long axis. The cavity tube now carries only the mixed contrast, so no iodine is counted twice. The shells (size scale 1, 1.4, 1.9 with iodine shares 0.5, 0.3, 0.2) give a soft edge. The puff is placed at the injecting catheter's tip (sceneBuilder passes the last point of catheterNodes or catheterRoot), clamped inside the cavity; without a tip it sits mid-cavity.
- **Parameters (LV_PUFF, all MODEL PARAMETERS):** concentration 0.5, elongation 1.6, at least 2 mL so it fades as it mixes rather than shrinking to a dot, at most 0.3 of cavity volume, not drawn below 0.01 mL. It decays with the existing LV_CAVITY.mixTauS.
- **Tests:** a 6 mL hand injection at 3 mL/s gives a central column above 3.5 mm of full-strength contrast and above 4 times the mixed cavity's mean column at 1.0 s and 1.6 s. Iodine is conserved within 1%, the puff follows the tip, and it is gone two beats after the push.
- **Not done:** the comparison against the pre-change baseline capture; no baseline capture was available to me.

Finding 4 (cavity density): applied as asked. The finding is logged in the lvGram.ts header as a MODEL PARAMETER for expert review, with the guidance to raise the cavity's iodine scaling rather than the mixing volumes, so the MR and AR tests are unchanged. No package notes file is among my editable files, so the note lives in the module header.

Finding 3: see rejected (outOfScope).
